claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth data in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: The importance of the Ded1 CTD is increased when either the Ded1-eIF4E or Ded1-eIF4A interactions are impaired.
claims.source: These findings are consistent with the idea that interaction of the Ded1 CTD with eIF4G is less critical for stabilizing the Ded1-eIF4E-eIF4A-eIF4G quaternary complex, activating Ded1 helicase function, or both, compared to the Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4E and eIF4A; but that the importance of the CTD is increased when either the Ded1-eIF4E or Ded1-eIF4A interactions are impaired.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth data in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: The eIF4A, eIF4E, and eIF4G1-HA all coimmunoprecipitated specifically with the myc13-tagged ded1-ts product.
claims.source: The eIF4A, eIF4E, and eIF4G1-HA all coimmunoprecipitated specifically with the myc13-tagged ded1-ts product, failing to be immunoprecipitated from the extract lacking a myc-tagged protein (Figure 5, rows 5–6), as expected for Ded1 interaction with eIF4F.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the coimmunoprecipitation experiment shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: The presence of mutations 21-27/51-57 in the ded1-ts allele reduced coimmunoprecipitation of the myc13-tagged product with native eIF4A, but not eIF4E or eIF4G1-HA from WCEs.
claims.source: The presence of mutations 21-27/51-57 in the ded1-ts allele, which impair Ded1 binding to GST-eIF4A in vitro (Figure 2B) reduced coimmunoprecipitation of the myc13-tagged product with native eIF4A, but not eIF4E or eIF4G1-HA from WCEs (Figure 5, rows 6–7).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the coimmunoprecipitation experiment shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: Mutations 59-65/83-89 specifically impaired coimmunoprecipition of eIF4E with the myc13-tagged ded1-ts/59-65/83-89 product.
claims.source: Moreover, mutations 59-65/83-89, which reduced Ded1 binding to GST-eIF4E in vitro (Figure 2C), specifically impaired coimmunoprecipition of eIF4E with the myc13-tagged ded1-ts/59-65/83-89 product (Figure 5, lanes 6 and 8).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the coimmunoprecipitation experiment shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: The coimmunoprecipitation results were unaffected by treating the immune complexes with RNAses A and T1, suggesting that the interactions are not bridged by RNA.
claims.source: The results were unaffected by treating the immune complexes with RNAses A and T1 (Figure 5, lanes 9–12 vs. 5–8), suggesting that the interactions are not bridged by RNA.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the coimmunoprecipitation experiment shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: The binding determinants in the Ded1 NTD for eIF4A and eIF4E defined by in vitro pull-down assays with recombinant GST fusions to eIF4A or eIF4E are also crucial for association of native eIF4A or eIF4E with the ded1-ts product expressed at native levels in yeast cells.
claims.source: Thus, the binding determinants in the Ded1 NTD for eIF4A and eIF4E defined by in vitro pull-down assays with recombinant GST fusions to eIF4A or eIF4E are also crucial for association of native eIF4A or eIF4E with the ded1-ts product expressed at native levels in yeast cells.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the coimmunoprecipitation data in Figure 5.

claims.claim: eIF4A overexpression mitigated the Slg- phenotypes at 34°C of the 21–27, 29–35, and 51–57 single-cluster mutations, and also the 21-27/29-35 double cluster mutations.
claims.source: eIF4A overexpression mitigated the Slg- phenotypes at 34°C of the 21–27, 29–35, and 51–57 single-cluster mutations, and also the 21-27/29-35 double cluster mutations (Figure 6B, rows 3–10, cf. adjacent rows), all of which conferred partial reductions in Ded1 binding to GST-eIF4A in vitro (Figure 2B), consistent with restored interaction of Ded1-eIF4A association by mass action.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: eIF4A overexpression did not mitigate the stronger Slg- phenotype conferred by the ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 double-cluster mutation.
claims.source: Importantly however, eIF4A overexpression did not mitigate the stronger Slg- phenotype conferred by the ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 double-cluster mutation (Figure 6B, rows 11–12), which reduced binding to GST-eIF4A to the low level conferred by the ΔN2-92 deletion that removes the entire eIF4A binding domain (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: eIF4A overexpression did not mitigate the Slg- phenotype conferred by the 59-65/83-89 mutations that selectively impair binding to eIF4E.
claims.source: Nor did eIF4A overexpression mitigate the Slg- phenotype conferred by the 59-65/83-89 mutations that selectively impair binding to eIF4E (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), supporting the interpretation that suppression of the other NTD mutations that partially impair eIF4A binding results from restoration of Ded1-eIF4A association by mass action (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Suppression of the NTD mutations that partially impair eIF4A binding by eIF4A overexpression results from restoration of Ded1-eIF4A association by mass action.
claims.source: Nor did eIF4A overexpression mitigate the Slg- phenotype conferred by the 59-65/83-89 mutations that selectively impair binding to eIF4E (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), supporting the interpretation that suppression of the other NTD mutations that partially impair eIF4A binding results from restoration of Ded1-eIF4A association by mass action (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Ded1 substitutions in the eIF4A-binding region of the NTD confer growth defects in vivo owing to impaired association with eIF4A in cells.
claims.source: These findings support the idea that Ded1 substitutions in the eIF4A-binding region of the NTD confer growth defects in vivo owing to impaired association with eIF4A in cells.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Overexpressing WT DED1 or the ded1-21-27/51-57 allele defective for eIF4A binding from a hc plasmid increased the growth rate of cdc33-1 cells.
claims.source: In agreement with this, we found that overexpressing either WT DED1 or the ded1-21-27/51-57 allele defective for eIF4A binding from a hc plasmid increased the growth rate of cdc33-1 cells (Figure 7A, rows 3–4 vs. 1.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: The hc ded1-59-65/83-89 allele, defective for eIF4E binding in vitro, had no effect on growth of the cdc33-1 mutant cells.
claims.source: Importantly, however, the hc ded1-59-65/83-89 allele, defective for eIF4E binding in vitro, had no effect on growth of the mutant cells (Figure 7A, row 5 vs. 1).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the growth assay shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: The ded1-59-65/83-89 mutation impairs both a physical and functional interaction between Ded1 and eIF4E in cells.
claims.source: These findings have two important implications. First, they provide strong evidence that the ded1-59-65/83-89 mutation impairs both a physical and functional interaction between Ded1 and eIF4E in cells.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth data in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: Overexpressing Ded1 partially suppresses the cdc33-1 mutation by enhancing interaction of the cdc33-1 product with Ded1 by mass action, presumably increasing the concentration of the eIF4F·Ded1 complex in which Ded1 functions most efficiently.
claims.source: Second, they imply that overexpressing Ded1 partially suppresses the cdc33-1 mutation by enhancing interaction of the cdc33-1 product with Ded1 by mass action, presumably increasing the concentration of the eIF4F·Ded1 complex in which Ded1 functions most efficiently, rather than indirectly compensating for a reduction in eIF4F function (that should occur for all ded1 alleles).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth data in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: Both the ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 and ded1-ts,59-65/83-89 mutations, impairing Ded1 interactions with eIF4A or eIF4E, respectively, reduced the ratio of polysomes to monosomes (P/M), indicating a reduction bulk translation initiation.
claims.source: Both the ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 and ded1-ts,59-65/83-89 mutations, impairing Ded1 interactions with eIF4A or eIF4E, respectively, reduced the ratio of polysomes to monosomes (P/M), indicating a reduction bulk translation initiation, which was not significantly greater for one mutation versus the other (Figure 8A).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome profiling shown in Figure 8A.

claims.claim: The reduction in P/M ratio conferred by ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 was not significantly greater than that conferred by ded1-ts,59-65/83-89.
claims.source: Both the ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 and ded1-ts,59-65/83-89 mutations, impairing Ded1 interactions with eIF4A or eIF4E, respectively, reduced the ratio of polysomes to monosomes (P/M), indicating a reduction bulk translation initiation, which was not significantly greater for one mutation versus the other (Figure 8A).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome profiling shown in Figure 8A.

claims.claim: Introducing single- or double-cluster NTD mutations that impair binding to eIF4A or eIF4E, or control NTD mutations 14–20 and 40–47 with no effect on eIF4A/eIF4E binding, had little or no effect on expression of the reporter lacking a 5'UTR SL.
claims.source: Relative to the ded1-ts parental mutant, introducing single- or double-cluster NTD mutations that impair binding to eIF4A or eIF4E, or control NTD mutations 14–20 and 40–47 with no effect on eIF4A/eIF4E binding, had little or no effect on expression of the reporter lacking a 5'UTR SL (Figure 8C, dark gray bars).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8C.

claims.claim: The reporter with a cap-distal SL showed reduced expression relative to the no-SL construct in the ded1-ts parental strain.
claims.source: The reporter with a cap-distal SL showed reduced expression relative to the no-SL construct in the ded1-ts parental strain (Figure 8—figure supplement 1, cols. 1–2), which was unaffected by the control NTD mutations; but was driven even lower by all of the mutations affecting eIF4A or eIF4E binding, with the greatest reductions seen for the two double substitutions ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 and ded1-ts,59-65/83-89 that eliminate, respectively, eIF4A or eIF4E binding to Ded1 (Figure 8C, light gray bars).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Expression of the cap-distal SL reporter was driven lower by all of the mutations affecting eIF4A or eIF4E binding, with the greatest reductions seen for the two double substitutions ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 and ded1-ts,59-65/83-89.
claims.source: The reporter with a cap-distal SL showed reduced expression relative to the no-SL construct in the ded1-ts parental strain (Figure 8—figure supplement 1, cols. 1–2), which was unaffected by the control NTD mutations; but was driven even lower by all of the mutations affecting eIF4A or eIF4E binding, with the greatest reductions seen for the two double substitutions ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 and ded1-ts,59-65/83-89 that eliminate, respectively, eIF4A or eIF4E binding to Ded1 (Figure 8C, light gray bars).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8C.

claims.claim: Expression of the cap-proximal SL reporter was reduced somewhat in the ded1-ts parental strain.
claims.source: Expression of the cap-proximal SL reporter was also reduced somewhat in the ded1-ts parental strain (Figure 8—figure supplement 1, col. 3 vs. 1), and was not further diminished by the control NTD mutations or the single cluster mutants defective for eIF4E binding (59–65 and 83–89), whereas the single cluster mutants defective for eIF4A binding (21–27 and 51–57) and both double-cluster mutants impairing eIF4A or eIF4E binding showed substantially reduced expression of this reporter, with the greatest reductions seen for the two double-cluster mutants (Figure 8C, white bars).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The single cluster mutants defective for eIF4A binding (21–27 and 51–57) and both double-cluster mutants impairing eIF4A or eIF4E binding showed substantially reduced expression of the cap-proximal SL reporter, with the greatest reductions seen for the two double-cluster mutants.
claims.source: Expression of the cap-proximal SL reporter was also reduced somewhat in the ded1-ts parental strain (Figure 8—figure supplement 1, col. 3 vs. 1), and was not further diminished by the control NTD mutations or the single cluster mutants defective for eIF4E binding (59–65 and 83–89), whereas the single cluster mutants defective for eIF4A binding (21–27 and 51–57) and both double-cluster mutants impairing eIF4A or eIF4E binding showed substantially reduced expression of this reporter, with the greatest reductions seen for the two double-cluster mutants (Figure 8C, white bars).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8C.

claims.claim: Overexpression of eIF4A conferred increased expression of the no SL and cap-distal reporters in the ded1-ts/21–27 mutant, predicted to exhibit partially impaired binding of eIF4A to Ded1, but not in the ded1-ts/21-27/51-57 or ded1-ts/59-65/83-89 strains.
claims.source: Interestingly, overexpression of eIF4A conferred increased expression of the no SL and cap-distal reporters in the ded1-ts/21–27 mutant, predicted to exhibit partially impaired binding of eIF4A to Ded1, but not in the ded1-ts/21-27/51-57 or ded1-ts/59-65/83-89 strains expected to be fully defective for eIF4A binding, or for eIF4E binding, respectively (Figure 8—figure supplement 5).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 5.

claims.claim: The defect in reporter expression conferred by ded1-ts/21–27 involved impaired Ded1 association with eIF4A.
claims.source: This supports the notion that the defect in reporter expression conferred by ded1-ts/21–27 involved impaired Ded1 association with eIF4A.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the luciferase assay data in Figure 8—figure supplement 5.

claims.claim: In the eIF4E-binding mutant ded1-ts,59-65/83-89, the proportion of reporter mRNA in the heavy polysome fractions is reduced, and the proportion in the smallest polysomes and monosomes is increased relative to the mRNA distribution in the parental strain.
claims.source: In the eIF4E-binding mutant ded1-ts,59-65/83-89, the proportion of reporter mRNA in the heavy polysome fractions is reduced, and the proportion in the smallest polysomes and monosomes is increased (Figure 8D (ii), orange points) relative to the mRNA distribution in the parental strain (Figure 8D (ii), grey points).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome distribution analysis shown in Figure 8D.

claims.claim: In the eIF4A binding mutant ded1-ts,21-27/51-57, the proportion of reporter mRNA in heavy polysomes is reduced and the proportion in free mRNP is elevated compared to that seen in the ded1-ts strain.
claims.source: Moreover, in the eIF4A binding mutant ded1-ts,21-27/51-57, the proportion of reporter mRNA in heavy polysomes is reduced and the proportion in free mRNP is elevated (Figure 8D (ii), green points) compared to that seen in the ded1-ts strain (Figure 8D (ii), grey points).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome distribution analysis shown in Figure 8D.

claims.claim: The more extensive shift from polysomes to free mRNP observed for the eIF4A-binding mutant compared to the shift from larger to smaller polysomes/monosomes conferred by the eIF4E-binding mutant is consistent with the relatively greater reductions in cap-proximal SL reporter expression given by the set of three eIF4A-binding mutants versus the three eIF4E-binding mutants.
claims.source: The more extensive shift from polysomes to free mRNP observed for the eIF4A-binding mutant compared to the shift from larger to smaller polysomes/monosomes conferred by the eIF4E-binding mutant (Figure 8D (ii), green vs. orange) is consistent with the relatively greater reductions in cap-proximal SL reporter expression given by the set of three eIF4A-binding mutants versus the three eIF4E-binding mutants (Figure 8C, eIF4A(-) vs. eIF4E(-) mutants).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by comparing the polysome distribution data in Figure 8D with the luciferase assay data in Figure 8C.

claims.claim: The polysome distribution of native ACT1 mRNA was not substantially altered by either of the Ded1 NTD mutations.
claims.source: In contrast to the behavior of the reporter mRNA, the polysome distribution of native ACT1 mRNA was not substantially altered by either of the Ded1 NTD mutations (Figure 8D (i)), suggesting that Ded1's interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E are relatively more important for the reporter mRNA harboring a stable SL structure compared to ACT1 mRNA.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome distribution analysis shown in Figure 8D.

claims.claim: Ded1's interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E are relatively more important for the reporter mRNA harboring a stable SL structure compared to ACT1 mRNA.
claims.source: In contrast to the behavior of the reporter mRNA, the polysome distribution of native ACT1 mRNA was not substantially altered by either of the Ded1 NTD mutations (Figure 8D (i)), suggesting that Ded1's interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E are relatively more important for the reporter mRNA harboring a stable SL structure compared to ACT1 mRNA.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the polysome distribution data in Figure 8D.

claims.claim: ACT1 mRNA was not found to be hyperdependent on Ded1 by ribosome profiling of a ded1 mutant.
claims.source: ACT1 mRNA was not found to be hyperdependent on Ded1 by ribosome profiling of a ded1 mutant (Sen et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a fact from prior work, supported by citation.

claims.claim: Loss of eIF4A and eIF4E interactions by the Ded1 NTD lead to reduced translation initiation of a Ded1-hyperdependent reporter mRNA, as well as to decreased bulk translation initiation in vivo.
claims.source: These results confirm that loss of eIF4A and eIF4E interactions by the Ded1 NTD lead to reduced translation initiation of a Ded1-hyperdependent reporter mRNA, as well as to decreased bulk translation initiation in vivo.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the polysome profiling and luciferase assay data in Figure 8.

claims.claim: The single amino acid mutations in the eIF4A binding region Y21A and R27A reduced expression of only the cap-distal SL (Y21A) or both SL reporters (R27A), compared to the parental ded1-ts strain.
claims.source: Assaying expression of the same LUC reporters, we found that the single amino acid mutations in the eIF4A binding region Y21A and R27A reduced expression of only the cap-distal SL (Y21A) or both SL reporters (R27A), and that the Y65A and W88A single-residue mutations in the eIF4E binding region reduced expression of both SL reporters, compared to the parental ded1-ts strain (Figure 8—figure supplement 1), thus supporting the importance of these individual residues in Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E in vivo.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The Y65A and W88A single-residue mutations in the eIF4E binding region reduced expression of both SL reporters, compared to the parental ded1-ts strain.
claims.source: Assaying expression of the same LUC reporters, we found that the single amino acid mutations in the eIF4A binding region Y21A and R27A reduced expression of only the cap-distal SL (Y21A) or both SL reporters (R27A), and that the Y65A and W88A single-residue mutations in the eIF4E binding region reduced expression of both SL reporters, compared to the parental ded1-ts strain (Figure 8—figure supplement 1), thus supporting the importance of these individual residues in Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E in vivo.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The 21-27/51-57/59-65/83-89 quadruple-cluster mutation and the Δ2–90 deletion of the NTD introduced into otherwise WT DED1 conferred nearly indistinguishable reductions in bulk polysome assembly.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2, the 21-27/51-57/59-65/83-89 quadruple-cluster mutation and the Δ2–90 deletion of the NTD introduced into otherwise WT DED1 conferred nearly indistinguishable reductions in bulk polysome assembly (panel A) and expression of both cap-proximal SL and cap-distal SL FLUC reporters (panel B).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome profiling shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: The 21-27/51-57/59-65/83-89 quadruple-cluster mutation and the Δ2–90 deletion of the NTD introduced into otherwise WT DED1 conferred nearly indistinguishable reductions in expression of both cap-proximal SL and cap-distal SL FLUC reporters.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2, the 21-27/51-57/59-65/83-89 quadruple-cluster mutation and the Δ2–90 deletion of the NTD introduced into otherwise WT DED1 conferred nearly indistinguishable reductions in bulk polysome assembly (panel A) and expression of both cap-proximal SL and cap-distal SL FLUC reporters (panel B).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: Eliminating both eIF4A and eIF4E binding simultaneously essentially inactivates the Ded1 NTD in promoting bulk translation as well as translation of Ded1-hyperdependent reporter mRNAs.
claims.source: We also provided evidence that eliminating both eIF4A and eIF4E binding simultaneously essentially inactivates the Ded1 NTD in promoting bulk translation as well as translation of Ded1-hyperdependent reporter mRNAs.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The ded1-ΔC mutation has little or no effect on polysome assembly on its own.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3A, the ded1-ΔC mutation analyzed above has little or no effect on polysome assembly on its own (cf. panels (i)-(ii)).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome profiling shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3A.

claims.claim: ΔC clearly exacerbates the effects of both the 21-27/51-57 and 59-65/83-89 double-cluster mutations in the Ded1 NTD in reducing P/M ratios, with a relatively greater effect for the 21-27/51-57 mutation that eliminates eIF4A binding.
claims.source: However, ΔC clearly exacerbates the effects of both the 21-27/51-57 and 59-65/83-89 double-cluster mutations in the Ded1 NTD in reducing P/M ratios, with a relatively greater effect for the 21-27/51-57 mutation that eliminates eIF4A binding (cf. (iii)-(iv) and (v)-(vi)).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the polysome profiling shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3A.

claims.claim: ded1-ΔC alone has only small effects on expression of the SL-containing FLUC reporters.
claims.source: Similarly, ded1-ΔC alone has only small effects on expression of the SL-containing FLUC reporters, but ΔC exacerbates the reductions in reporter expression conferred by 21-27/51-57 (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B, set four vs. sets 2 and 3) and by the 59-65/83-89 mutation (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B, set six vs. sets 2 and 5).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3B.

claims.claim: ΔC exacerbates the reductions in reporter expression conferred by 21-27/51-57 and by the 59-65/83-89 mutation.
claims.source: Similarly, ded1-ΔC alone has only small effects on expression of the SL-containing FLUC reporters, but ΔC exacerbates the reductions in reporter expression conferred by 21-27/51-57 (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B, set four vs. sets 2 and 3) and by the 59-65/83-89 mutation (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B, set six vs. sets 2 and 5).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the luciferase assay shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3B.

claims.claim: Eliminating eIF4G association with the Ded1 CTD imposes a relatively greater requirement for the Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E, either in forming or stabilizing the eIF4F·Ded1 complex or in stimulating Ded1 unwinding activity.
claims.source: These findings support our conclusion that eliminating eIF4G association with the Ded1 CTD imposes a relatively greater requirement for the Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E, either in forming or stabilizing the eIF4F·Ded1 complex or in stimulating Ded1 unwinding activity.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: FL Ded1 substantially increased the kmax of 48S PIC formation on CP-8.1 mRNA by ~5 fold compared to the absence of Ded1.
claims.source: In agreement with previous results (Gupta et al., 2018), FL Ded1 substantially increased the kmax of 48S PIC formation on CP-8.1 mRNA by ~5 fold compared to the absence of Ded1, and deleting the NTD diminished the rate enhancement conferred by addition of Ded1 compared to no Ded1 in the reaction by ≈60% (Figure 9A, cols. 1–3; see Figure 9—figure supplement 1C for data summary).

claims.claim: Deleting the NTD diminished the rate enhancement conferred by addition of Ded1 compared to no Ded1 in the reaction by ≈60% on CP-8.1 mRNA.
claims.source: In agreement with previous results (Gupta et al., 2018), FL Ded1 substantially increased the kmax of 48S PIC formation on CP-8.1 mRNA by ~5 fold compared to the absence of Ded1, and deleting the NTD diminished the rate enhancement conferred by addition of Ded1 compared to no Ded1 in the reaction by ≈60% (Figure 9A, cols. 1–3; see Figure 9—figure supplement 1C for data summary).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9A.

claims.claim: Disrupting eIF4A binding to the NTD with the 21-27/51-57 double substitutions was comparable to the ΔNTD1-116 in reducing kmax on CP-8.1 mRNA.
claims.source: Interestingly, disrupting eIF4A binding to the NTD with the 21-27/51-57 double substitutions was comparable to the ΔNTD1-116 in reducing kmax, whereas the 59–65 substitution that affects eIF4E binding had no effect on the kmax (Figure 9A, cols. 3–5).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9A.

claims.claim: The 59–65 substitution that affects eIF4E binding had no effect on the kmax on CP-8.1 mRNA.
claims.source: Interestingly, disrupting eIF4A binding to the NTD with the 21-27/51-57 double substitutions was comparable to the ΔNTD1-116 in reducing kmax, whereas the 59–65 substitution that affects eIF4E binding had no effect on the kmax (Figure 9A, cols. 3–5).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9A.

claims.claim: The ΔNTD1-116 truncation greatly increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on CP-8.1 mRNA.
claims.source: The ΔNTD1-116 truncation also greatly increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on this mRNA (Figure 9B, cols. 1–2), as observed previously (Gupta et al., 2018); and both the 21-27/51-57 and 59–65 substitutions also increased the K1/2 for Ded1 to an extent ≈40% of that given by the ΔNTD1-116 (Figure 9B, cols. 2–4).

claims.claim: Both the 21-27/51-57 and 59–65 substitutions increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on CP-8.1 mRNA to an extent ≈40% of that given by the ΔNTD1-116.

claims.claim: FL Ded1 increased the kmax for RPL41A mRNA by ~3 fold.

claims.claim: Eliminating the Ded1 NTD by ΔNTD1-116 did not impair the stimulation of kmax on RPL41A mRNA.
claims.source: As observed previously (Gupta et al., 2018), FL Ded1 increased the kmax for RPL41A mRNA by ~3 fold, and eliminating the Ded1 NTD by ΔNTD1-116 did not impair this stimulation (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A, cols. 2–3); however, ΔNTD1-116 increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on RPL41A mRNA by nearly 70-fold (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, cols. 2–3).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: ΔNTD1-116 increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on RPL41A mRNA by nearly 70-fold.
claims.source: As observed previously (Gupta et al., 2018), FL Ded1 increased the kmax for RPL41A mRNA by ~3 fold, and eliminating the Ded1 NTD by ΔNTD1-116 did not impair this stimulation (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A, cols. 2–3); however, ΔNTD1-116 increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on RPL41A mRNA by nearly 70-fold (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, cols. 2–3).

claims.source: As expected, neither the 21-27/51-57 double substitution nor the 59–65 substitution altered the increase in kmax for RPL41A mRNA conferred by FL Ded1 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A, cols. 4–5 vs. 2).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Both the 21-27/51-57 and 59–65 substitutions increased the K1/2 for Ded1 on RPL41A mRNA (~7 fold for 21-27/51-57 and ~4 fold for the 59–65 substitution), but these increases were much smaller than the ~70 fold increase produced by ΔNTD1-116.
claims.source: While both substitutions increased the K1/2 for Ded1 compared to FL-Ded1 (~7 fold for 21-27/51-57 and ~4 fold for the 59–65 substitution), these increases were much smaller than the ~70 fold increase produced by ΔNTD1-116 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, cols. 3–4 vs. 2 cf. col.1;and Figure 9—figure supplement 1D, cols. 4–5 vs. 2 cf. col. 1).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstituted system assay shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Strong interaction of either eIF4A or eIF4E with the Ded1-NTD is sufficient to greatly reduce the amount of Ded1 required for maximum acceleration of 48S PIC assembly on RPL41A mRNA.
claims.source: These last results suggest that strong interaction of either eIF4A or eIF4E with the Ded1-NTD is sufficient to greatly reduce the amount of Ded1 required for maximum acceleration of 48S PIC assembly on RPL41A mRNA.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the reconstituted system data in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: On CP-8.1 mRNA, eliminating either of the interactions of the Ded1-NTD with eIF4A and eIF4E conferred an increase in the Ded1 K1/2 only slightly smaller than that given by deleting the entire NTD.
claims.source: This contrasts with our findings on CP-8.1 mRNA, where eliminating either of the interactions of the Ded1-NTD with eIF4A and eIF4E conferred an increase in the Ded1 K1/2 only slightly smaller than that given by deleting the entire NTD.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by comparing the reconstituted system data for CP-8.1 mRNA in Figure 9B with that for RPL41A mRNA in Figure 9—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Both interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E are needed simultaneously to enhance the function of the eIF4F-Ded1 complex on the more structured CP-8.1 mRNA, whereas each interaction can contribute independently and additively on the less structured RPL41A mRNA.
claims.source: Thus, it appears that both interactions are needed simultaneously to enhance the function of the eIF4F-Ded1 complex on the more structured CP-8.1 mRNA, whereas each interaction can contribute independently and additively on the less structured RPL41A mRNA.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by comparing the reconstituted system data for CP-8.1 mRNA in Figure 9 with that for RPL41A mRNA in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The Ded1 NTD interacts directly with eIF4E and eIF4A via adjacent, non-overlapping segments of the NTD.
claims.source: Together, our findings indicate that the Ded1 NTD interacts directly with eIF4E and eIF4A via adjacent, non-overlapping segments of the NTD, and that these interactions, in concert with the Ded1-CTD interaction with eIF4G, make independent, additive contributions to Ded1 function in stimulating translation initiation in vivo.
claims.evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claims.claim: The Ded1 NTD interactions with eIF4E and eIF4A, in concert with the Ded1-CTD interaction with eIF4G, make independent, additive contributions to Ded1 function in stimulating translation initiation in vivo.
claims.source: Together, our findings indicate that the Ded1 NTD interacts directly with eIF4E and eIF4A via adjacent, non-overlapping segments of the NTD, and that these interactions, in concert with the Ded1-CTD interaction with eIF4G, make independent, additive contributions to Ded1 function in stimulating translation initiation in vivo.
claims.evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claims.claim: In all in vivo assays of cell growth and bulk or reporter mRNA translation, eliminating Ded1 interaction with eIF4G by deleting the Ded1 CTD had a less severe impact than did impairing eIF4A or eIF4E binding to the Ded1 NTD.
claims.source: As summarized schematically in Figure 9D, in all of our in vivo assays of cell growth and bulk or reporter mRNA translation, eliminating Ded1 interaction with eIF4G by deleting the Ded1 CTD had a less severe impact than did impairing eIF4A or eIF4E binding to the Ded1 NTD, and the eIF4A interaction with Ded1 appeared to be the most important overall.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from multiple in vivo assays throughout the manuscript.

claims.claim: The eIF4A interaction with Ded1 appeared to be the most important overall for Ded1 function in vivo.
claims.source: As summarized schematically in Figure 9D, in all of our in vivo assays of cell growth and bulk or reporter mRNA translation, eliminating Ded1 interaction with eIF4G by deleting the Ded1 CTD had a less severe impact than did impairing eIF4A or eIF4E binding to the Ded1 NTD, and the eIF4A interaction with Ded1 appeared to be the most important overall.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from multiple in vivo assays throughout the manuscript.

claims.claim: All of the Ded1 interactions with eIF4F subunits should serve to tether Ded1 tightly to the activated eIF4F·mRNA complex and focus its helicase activity on the 5'UTR to unwind structures that impede PIC attachment or subsequent scanning.
claims.source: Envisioning all of these interactions occurring simultaneously on an mRNA suggests that they should serve to tether Ded1 tightly to the activated eIF4F·mRNA complex and focus its helicase activity on the 5'UTR to unwind structures that impede PIC attachment or subsequent scanning (Figure 9C).
claims.evidence: This is a model proposed to explain the data, depicted in Figure 9C.

claims.claim: The Ded1-NTD interaction with eIF4A is particularly important for enhancing Ded1 unwinding of the SL structure in CP-8.1 mRNA.
claims.source: Consistent with previous in vitro findings that interaction with eIF4A increases Ded1 unwinding activity (Gao et al., 2016), our results here in the reconstituted system suggest that the Ded1-NTD interaction with eIF4A is particularly important for enhancing Ded1 unwinding of the SL structure in CP-8.1 mRNA.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the reconstituted system data in Figure 9A, supported by prior work.

claims.claim: Ded1-NTD interactions with both eIF4A and eIF4E, and Ded1-CTD binding to eIF4G, all help to assemble and stabilize the eIF4F-Ded1 complex at the 5' ends of mRNAs, which enhances initiation of nearly all mRNAs.
claims.source: In summary, we envision that Ded1-NTD interactions with both eIF4A and eIF4E, and Ded1-CTD binding to eIF4G, all help to assemble and stabilize the eIF4F-Ded1 complex at the 5' ends of mRNAs, which enhances initiation of nearly all mRNAs, whereas the Ded1-NTD/eIF4A interaction is additionally important to stimulate Ded1 unwinding of strong secondary structures in mRNA 5'UTRs (Figure 9C).
claims.evidence: This is a summary model proposed to explain the data, depicted in Figure 9C.

claims.claim: The Ded1-NTD/eIF4A interaction is additionally important to stimulate Ded1 unwinding of strong secondary structures in mRNA 5'UTRs.
claims.source: In summary, we envision that Ded1-NTD interactions with both eIF4A and eIF4E, and Ded1-CTD binding to eIF4G, all help to assemble and stabilize the eIF4F-Ded1 complex at the 5' ends of mRNAs, which enhances initiation of nearly all mRNAs, whereas the Ded1-NTD/eIF4A interaction is additionally important to stimulate Ded1 unwinding of strong secondary structures in mRNA 5'UTRs (Figure 9C).
claims.evidence: This is a summary model proposed to explain the data, depicted in Figure 9C.

claims.claim: The stimulation of Ded1 unwinding by eIF4A might also involve eIF4A molecules not tethered to eIF4F at the cap structure, given the much greater abundance of eIF4A compared to eIF4E and eIF4G.
claims.source: Given the much greater abundance of eIF4A compared to eIF4E and eIF4G (von der Haar and McCarthy, 2002), the stimulation of Ded1 unwinding by eIF4A might also involve eIF4A molecules not tethered to eIF4F at the cap structure.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on known protein abundances.

results.result: Full-length Ded1 binds specifically to both GST-eIF4A and GST-eIF4E in vitro, and this binding requires the Ded1 N-terminal domain (NTD) for eIF4A interaction.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C57 demonstrate through GST pull-down assays (Figure 1B-C) that FL Ded1 binds both eIF4A and eIF4E, but not GST alone, and that deletion of the NTD (ΔN2-92) drastically reduces eIF4A binding while the CTD deletion does not affect eIF4A binding. This provides clear evidence for specific NTD-mediated eIF4A interaction.

results.result: The Ded1 NTD is considerably more important than the CTD for eIF4E binding, providing the first evidence that eIF4E binds directly to the yeast Ded1 NTD.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C63 are supported by GST pull-down data (Figure 1D) showing that NTD deletion reduces eIF4E binding more than CTD deletion, and that the double deletion (ΔNC) does not further reduce binding beyond ΔN2-92 alone. This establishes the NTD as the primary eIF4E binding site.

results.result: The Ded1 CTD is essential for binding to eIF4G but dispensable for eIF4A interaction and relatively unimportant for eIF4E interaction.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C68 are supported by GST pull-down data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) showing that ΔC562-604 abolishes eIF4G binding but has minimal effect on eIF4A binding (Figure 1C) and modest effect on eIF4E binding (Figure 1D). This establishes distinct binding requirements for different eIF4F subunits.

results.result: Specific amino acid clusters in the Ded1 NTD mediate binding to eIF4A (residues 21-57) or eIF4E (residues 59-89) in non-overlapping regions.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C75 are supported by systematic mutagenesis and GST pull-down assays (Figure 2B-C) showing that substitutions in residues 21-27, 29-35, and 51-57 reduce eIF4A binding, while substitutions in residues 59-65 and 83-89 reduce eIF4E binding. This fine-mapping identifies distinct binding determinants.

results.result: Non-contiguous substitutions 21-27 and 51-57 have additive effects on eIF4A binding, with the double mutant showing binding defects comparable to complete NTD deletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C78 are supported by GST pull-down data (Figure 2B) showing that combining 21-27 with 51-57 produces additive binding defects equivalent to ΔN2-92, while combining contiguous substitutions 21-27 and 29-35 does not. This demonstrates that multiple non-overlapping regions contribute to eIF4A binding.

results.result: The binding determinants for eIF4A and eIF4E are segregated into non-overlapping adjacent segments of the Ded1 NTD, with mutations selectively affecting one interaction but not the other.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C82 are supported by GST pull-down data (Figure 2B-C) showing that double substitutions 21-27/51-57 and 59-65/83-89 selectively impair eIF4A or eIF4E binding respectively without affecting the other interaction. This demonstrates functional segregation of binding sites.

results.result: Single amino acid substitutions R27A, Y65A, and W88A recapitulate the binding defects of their respective cluster mutations, with R27 and W88 being highly conserved residues critical for eIF4A and eIF4E binding respectively.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C98 are supported by single-residue mutagenesis data (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B-C) showing that R27A impairs eIF4A binding to the same extent as the 21-27 cluster, while Y65A and W88A impair eIF4E binding equivalently to their respective clusters. Conservation analysis supports the functional importance of these residues.

results.result: NTD substitutions that impair eIF4A or eIF4E binding in vitro confer slow-growth phenotypes in vivo when combined with ded1-ts, with eIF4A-binding mutations showing stronger effects than eIF4E-binding mutations.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C104 are supported by growth assays (Figure 3B) showing that mutations impairing eIF4A binding (21-27, 51-57, 21-27/51-57) confer stronger growth defects than those impairing eIF4E binding (59-65, 83-89, 59-65/83-89), while control mutations have no effect. Western blots confirm these effects are not due to reduced expression.

results.result: The quadruple mutation 21-27/51-57/59-65/83-89 that eliminates both eIF4A and eIF4E binding confers a growth defect comparable to complete NTD deletion, suggesting that eIF4A/eIF4E binding constitutes the key in vivo function of the Ded1 NTD.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C116 are supported by growth assays (Figure 3C) showing that the quadruple mutation and Δ2-90 deletion produce equivalent severe growth defects, and Western blots confirm similar expression levels. This provides strong evidence that eIF4A/eIF4E binding is the primary NTD function.

results.result: Deletion of the Ded1 CTD exacerbates the growth defects of NTD mutations that impair eIF4A or eIF4E binding, revealing that the CTD becomes more important when NTD interactions are compromised.
results.evaluation: Claims C118-C122 are supported by growth assays (Figure 4A) showing that ΔC exacerbates growth defects of NTD mutations, particularly for 21-27 and double-cluster substitutions, without reducing protein expression (Figure 4B). This demonstrates functional redundancy and compensation between Ded1 domains.

results.result: NTD mutations that impair eIF4A or eIF4E binding in vitro also selectively reduce coimmunoprecipitation of native eIF4A or eIF4E with Ded1 in vivo, confirming the physiological relevance of these binding determinants.
results.evaluation: Claims C123-C127 are supported by coimmunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 5) showing that 21-27/51-57 mutations reduce eIF4A but not eIF4E/eIF4G coIP, while 59-65/83-89 mutations reduce eIF4E but not eIF4A/eIF4G coIP. RNase treatment confirms these are protein-protein interactions.

results.result: Overexpression of eIF4A suppresses growth defects of NTD mutations that partially impair eIF4A binding but not those that completely abolish eIF4A binding or those that impair eIF4E binding, demonstrating that growth defects result from impaired Ded1-eIF4A association.
results.evaluation: Claims C128-C132 are supported by genetic suppression experiments (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1) showing selective rescue of partial eIF4A-binding mutants by eIF4A overexpression. This provides strong genetic evidence that the NTD mutations function by disrupting specific protein-protein interactions.

results.result: Overexpression of WT Ded1 or the eIF4A-binding mutant ded1-21-27/51-57 suppresses the cdc33-1 (eIF4E) mutant, but the eIF4E-binding mutant ded1-59-65/83-89 does not, demonstrating that Ded1-eIF4E interaction is functionally important in vivo.
results.evaluation: Claims C133-C136 are supported by genetic suppression experiments (Figure 7A) showing differential rescue of cdc33-1 by different Ded1 variants, with Western blots confirming similar expression levels (Figure 7B). This provides reciprocal genetic evidence for the functional importance of Ded1-eIF4E interaction.

results.result: Both eIF4A-binding and eIF4E-binding mutations in the Ded1 NTD reduce bulk polysome assembly to similar extents, indicating reduced translation initiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C137-C138 are supported by polysome profiling (Figure 8A) showing that both ded1-ts,21-27/51-57 and ded1-ts,59-65/83-89 reduce P/M ratios compared to parental ded1-ts, with no significant difference between the two mutants. This demonstrates that both interactions contribute to bulk translation.

results.result: NTD mutations that impair eIF4A or eIF4E binding preferentially reduce translation of reporter mRNAs with structured 5'UTRs, with eIF4A-binding mutations showing stronger effects on cap-proximal stem-loop reporters.
results.evaluation: Claims C139-C143 are supported by luciferase reporter assays (Figure 8C, Figure 8—figure supplement 1) showing that NTD mutations have minimal effect on unstructured reporters but reduce expression of structured reporters, with eIF4A-binding mutations showing the strongest effects on cap-proximal SL reporters.

results.result: The eIF4A-binding mutant shows a more extensive shift of reporter mRNA from polysomes to free mRNP compared to the eIF4E-binding mutant, consistent with the greater reduction in cap-proximal SL reporter expression by eIF4A-binding mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C146-C148 are supported by polysome distribution analysis (Figure 8D) showing differential effects of the two mutants on reporter mRNA distribution, with the eIF4A-binding mutant causing greater accumulation in free mRNP. This correlates with the luciferase data and demonstrates distinct mechanistic roles.

results.result: The polysome distribution of native ACT1 mRNA is not substantially altered by NTD mutations, suggesting that Ded1 interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E are relatively more important for structured reporter mRNAs than for Ded1-hypodependent native mRNAs.
results.evaluation: Claims C149-C152 are supported by polysome distribution analysis (Figure 8D) showing that ACT1 mRNA distribution is unaffected by NTD mutations that alter reporter mRNA distribution. This is consistent with prior ribosome profiling data showing ACT1 is not Ded1-hyperdependent.

results.result: The quadruple-cluster mutation 21-27/51-57/59-65/83-89 and the Δ2-90 NTD deletion produce nearly indistinguishable reductions in bulk polysome assembly and reporter mRNA translation, demonstrating that eIF4A/eIF4E binding essentially accounts for all NTD function in translation.
results.evaluation: Claims C155-C157 are supported by polysome profiling and luciferase assays (Figure 8—figure supplement 2) showing equivalent defects for the quadruple mutation and NTD deletion. This provides strong functional evidence that eIF4A/eIF4E binding is the primary NTD function.

results.result: The CTD deletion (ΔC) exacerbates the effects of NTD mutations on polysome assembly and reporter translation, with greater effects for the eIF4A-binding mutant, demonstrating that eliminating eIF4G association increases the requirement for NTD interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E.
results.evaluation: Claims C158-C162 are supported by polysome profiling and luciferase assays (Figure 8—figure supplement 3) showing that ΔC alone has minimal effects but exacerbates NTD mutation phenotypes. This demonstrates functional compensation between Ded1 domains in translation.

results.result: In the reconstituted system, FL Ded1 increases the kmax of 48S PIC formation on CP-8.1 mRNA by ~5-fold, and disrupting eIF4A binding (21-27/51-57) reduces kmax comparably to NTD deletion, while disrupting eIF4E binding (59-65) has no effect on kmax.
results.evaluation: Claims C163-C166 are supported by reconstituted system kinetic assays (Figure 9A) showing differential effects of NTD mutations on kmax for CP-8.1 mRNA. This demonstrates that eIF4A interaction is specifically required for maximum rate enhancement on structured mRNAs.

results.result: Both the 21-27/51-57 and 59-65 substitutions increase the K1/2 for Ded1 on CP-8.1 mRNA to ~40% of the increase given by complete NTD deletion, indicating that both interactions contribute to efficient Ded1 recruitment.
results.evaluation: Claims C167-C168 are supported by reconstituted system kinetic assays (Figure 9B) showing that both NTD mutations increase K1/2, though less than complete NTD deletion. This demonstrates that both eIF4A and eIF4E interactions enhance Ded1 function on structured mRNAs.

results.result: On the less structured RPL41A mRNA, NTD deletion increases K1/2 by ~70-fold, but individual disruption of eIF4A or eIF4E binding increases K1/2 by only ~4-7 fold, suggesting that strong interaction with either factor is sufficient for efficient Ded1 function on unstructured mRNAs.
results.evaluation: Claims C171-C176 are supported by reconstituted system kinetic assays (Figure 9—figure supplement 1) showing differential effects of NTD mutations on RPL41A versus CP-8.1 mRNA. This demonstrates that structured and unstructured mRNAs have different requirements for Ded1-eIF4F interactions.

results.result: Both eIF4A and eIF4E interactions are needed simultaneously to enhance Ded1 function on the structured CP-8.1 mRNA, whereas each interaction can contribute independently on the less structured RPL41A mRNA.
results.evaluation: Claims C177-C178 are supported by comparing reconstituted system data for CP-8.1 (Figure 9B) and RPL41A (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B) mRNAs, showing different patterns of K1/2 increases for single versus double mutations. This demonstrates mRNA-specific requirements for Ded1-eIF4F interactions.

results.result: The Ded1 NTD interacts directly with eIF4E and eIF4A via adjacent, non-overlapping segments, and these interactions, together with Ded1-CTD interaction with eIF4G, make independent, additive contributions to Ded1 function in stimulating translation initiation in vivo.
results.evaluation: Claims C179-C180 represent the main conclusion of the study, supported by the comprehensive set of in vitro binding, in vivo functional, and reconstituted system data throughout the manuscript. The evidence demonstrates distinct binding sites with independent functional contributions.

results.result: In all in vivo assays, eliminating Ded1-eIF4G interaction by CTD deletion has less severe impact than impairing eIF4A or eIF4E binding to the NTD, with the eIF4A interaction appearing most important overall.
results.evaluation: Claims C181-C182 are supported by the comprehensive in vivo data (Figures 3-8) showing consistent patterns across growth, polysome, and reporter assays. This establishes a hierarchy of importance for Ded1-eIF4F interactions in vivo.

results.result: A model is proposed where Ded1-NTD interactions with eIF4A and eIF4E, and Ded1-CTD binding to eIF4G, tether Ded1 to the eIF4F·mRNA complex to enhance initiation of nearly all mRNAs, while the Ded1-NTD/eIF4A interaction additionally stimulates unwinding of strong secondary structures.
results.evaluation: Claims C183-C186 represent a mechanistic model (Figure 9C) that integrates the in vitro, in vivo, and reconstituted system data. The model is well-supported by the differential effects of mutations on structured versus unstructured mRNAs and the correlation with prior biochemical data on Ded1 unwinding activity.
